# ECN-2026-043 - Change notice - Machining CNC turning center #3

Revision: Rev A  
Plant: P1, line P1-L3  
Equipment: EQ-P1-L3-CN03

## Reason for change
Background: During routine commissioning and subsequent process qualification of EQ-P1-L3-CN03 it was observed that the existing warm-up procedure did not reliably achieve stable spindle thermal conditions prior to production start. Process drift at the beginning of a run led to sporadic dimensional excursions on first-piece outputs traced to spindle thermal transient. The change clarifies and standardizes the spindle warm-up requirement to eliminate variability and to align operator practice with the capability observed during machine vendor validation and internal trial runs.

Rationale: Specifying a defined spindle warm-up time reduces operator ambiguity, prevents premature loading of parts, and provides a documented control to support first-article quality. The change is intended to reduce rework and inspection burden at the line level and to ensure consistent part geometry from start-of-run pieces. This ECN also aligns shop procedure with recorded best practice from the process trials summarized in SB-1014.

Related documents: implement this change consistent with SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, and SOP-P1-L3-03.

## Affected items
Scope: This ECN applies specifically to Machining CNC turning center #3, equipment id EQ-P1-L3-CN03, located on line P1-L3 at plant P1. It affects operator start-of-shift activities, first-article production sequences, in-process inspection checkpoints tied to initial production pieces, and the machine log entry procedure.

Affected artifacts and records:
- Operator machine start checklist for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 referenced in SOP-P1-L3-02.
- First-article inspection records retained per SOP-P1-L3-03.
- Machine maintenance and event log entries referenced in SB-1014.

Examples of affected activities:
- Pre-production machine preparation steps that currently omit a standardized spindle run-in.
- First-piece verification where measurement is taken immediately after initial loading without consideration for spindle thermal stabilization.

## Implementation
Change description: Update the machine start procedure for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to require a spindle warm-up period of 27 minutes prior to loading production parts. This requirement is to be added to the operator checklist in SOP-P1-L3-02 and to be referenced in the first-article instruction in SOP-P1-L3-03. The warm-up is an active step: the spindle is run under the conditions specified in the machine control recipe for warm-up as documented in SB-1014, and operators shall not load production parts onto the chuck until the warm-up time is complete.

Step-by-step implementation tasks:
- Revise the operator checklist entry in SOP-P1-L3-02 to include: "Run spindle warm-up for 27 minutes; do not load production parts until complete."
- Update first-article instructions in SOP-P1-L3-03 to require that first-article sampling begins only after the warm-up procedure is completed and documented.
- Revise operator training materials and on-shop-floor quick reference for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to reflect the new requirement.
- Add a field to the machine log for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 to record start time and completion confirmation of the 27 minutes warm-up period in the machine event log governed by SB-1014.

Operator actions and examples:
- Example scenario: prior to a production shift, the operator performs machine safety checks and coolant verification per SOP-P1-L3-02, then initiates the spindle warm-up procedure and observes the spindle run indicators for the 27 minutes before proceeding to load the first raw blank.
- Example scenario: when a short trial run is required for program verification, the operator must still perform the 27 minutes warm-up and record the activity in the machine event log before producing verification pieces.

Records to keep:
- Machine event log entry for each warm-up showing equipment id EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and affirmation that the 27 minutes warm-up was completed; retain per SB-1014.
- First-article inspection record with timestamped note that inspection occurred after completion of the warm-up; file under the production batch per SOP-P1-L3-03.
- Training completion acknowledgment for operators assigned to EQ-P1-L3-CN03 indicating awareness and adherence to the warm-up requirement; file per existing training records practice.

Nonconforming condition handling:
- If an operator inadvertently loads parts before the 27 minutes warm-up is complete, immediate actions include halting production, segregating affected pieces, and initiating first-article inspection per SOP-P1-L3-03. All incidents must be recorded in the machine log and escalated to line supervision for disposition in accordance with SB-1014.

Timing and rollout:
- Owners: Machine steward for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 is responsible for updating SOP-P1-L3-02 and coordinating training. Quality owner to update SOP-P1-L3-03 references and inspection triggers. Documentation updates must reference SB-1014 for log retention practices.

Verification:
- After implementation, the first production shift will include confirmation that machine logs contain entries for the 27 minutes warm-up for EQ-P1-L3-CN03 and that first-article inspections were performed post-warm-up. Deviations will be recorded in SB-1014.

## Approvals
Review and approval required from the following functions prior to release of revised SOP-P1-L3-02 and SOP-P1-L3-03 and shop-floor changes:
- Production lead for line P1-L3
- Quality assurance owner for P1 operations
- Maintenance steward for EQ-P1-L3-CN03

Document references for approval: SB-1014, SOP-P1-L3-02, SOP-P1-L3-03

Approval signatures and dates will be recorded in the ECN control sheet and associated revision log maintained per SB-1014.
